hook.line: Excuse me mate, what do you do for work? I work in digital marketing.
hook.visual: A man walks down an office corridor looking at his phone and is stopped by an off-camera street-interview style question; small native captions under his face.

beats.what: Street-interview parody: Chris is stopped in the corridor and asked what he does.
Smash cut to a colour-tinted title card: 'CHRIS' in a slanted banner, film-credits style.
Red tint, 'Chris as Social Media Manager', filming himself on his phone.
Blue tint, 'Email Marketer', slumped over a laptop.
Orange tint, 'Influencer Manager', shouting into a phone.
Yellow, 'Graphic Designer'; then red 'Content Creator' with a shocked face.
Split frame: 'Confused Chris' and 'Happy Chris' side by side.
Orange, 'Copy Writer', at a laptop; cut to black end card.

characters.who: Chris, an employee playing every marketing role
characters.enters: Walks into frame down a corridor, looking at his phone, then is stopped by the interviewer.
characters.acts: Answers one question, then reappears in a rapid montage of one-pose role vignettes, each with its own colour tint and slanted name banner.
characters.exits: The last vignette cuts to a black end card.

why_it_works: Familiar street-interview format in the first second, then a hard break into a mock film-credits montage, so the twist lands as a surprise.
Each role is one exaggerated pose shown for under a second (median shot 0.86 s), so the joke is 'one person does everything' and marketers tag colleagues.
Consistent kit per vignette (new colour tint plus the same slanted banner with 'CHRIS as ...') makes a fast montage readable at a glance.
Speech stops after ~4 s; the rest is music and titles, so it works muted.
weaknesses: No teaching or product, so it builds brand affinity but no reason to follow for value.
Ends on a black card with no payoff line or CTA, which wastes the last second.
for_robert: Use the 'cast credits' montage: give Fred a slanted name banner per role ('Fred as SEO', 'Fred as copywriter') with a new background colour each beat, under a second apiece.
